## Mend 1.0.13 — 15 Oct 2026

- **Releases build in a fraction of the time, all on the Mac, with Pour:** every Rust build cache now lives *outside* the project folder — the Mac and Windows targets in `/Users/Shared/mend-build/target` (`MEND_BUILD_CACHE=` to move it), Linux in the Docker volumes `mend-target-<arch>`, `mend-cargo-<arch>` and `mend-npm` — so a freshly unzipped source still builds incrementally (only Mend itself recompiles: about a minute per target instead of 8–10). The web app is built once and every `tauri build` reuses `dist/`. The two Linux builds run in the background while the Mac and Windows installers build (`--serial` to run them afterwards; the log is kept in `.release-cache/linux-build.log`). The build tools (nsis, llvm, docker, colima, node, gh…) are installed with **Pour** — Homebrew is never required; it is used only as a last resort when it happens to be present and Pour could not install something. Both GitHub repos get the full **20 topics** GitHub allows (`scripts/repo-details.sh` trims longer lists and warns about shorter ones).
- **Pour everywhere in the app too:** Helpers & Log installs libimobiledevice, ideviceinstaller, ipatool, smartmontools, Android platform-tools and pipx with `pour install` (Pour is installed first when it is missing — never Homebrew), the idevicerestore build script uses Pour's formulae, and Mend's search path includes Pour's bin folders (`POUR_PREFIX`, `~/.pour/bin`, `/opt/pour/bin`).
- **Dock + menu bar: closing the last window quits.** Whenever Mend is in the Dock — “Dock only” *or* “Dock and menu bar” — closing the last window or tab ends Mend completely, like any Mac app. Only “Menu bar only” and “Background” can keep running after the window closes (Settings says so next to the choice).
- **Settings → Updates:** the current version, **Check for updates now**, when the last check ran, and a switch for the check at start-up. A found update is also announced with a desktop notification.
- **The menu-bar icon has two pop-ups:** a **left click** opens a compact *quick panel* under the icon (connected devices, disks with their health, twelve one-click actions, Hide window, Quit; it closes when it loses focus or with Esc; a double-click opens the whole window) and a **right click** opens the full menu, now with a status line (devices · disks · lowest health), Quick Panel, *Quick Fixes* (flush DNS, repair the network, restart sound/Bluetooth/the desktop, rebuild search, permissions, fonts, icons, print queue, clock, system files, updates, disk/memory/sleep questions — each mapped to the right repair for this system), *Repair* (now with a short self-test on every disk and TRIM every SSD), *Back up*, *Contacts* (scan, AI tidy, export every account, import), *Mend AI*, *Appearance*, *Animations*, *Language*, *Mend Lives In*, *Window & Help* (show/hide, compact or large window, sidebar, check for updates, about, shortcuts, star on GitHub, logs, crash reports), Settings, Mend Pro and Quit. The same groups appear in the **Dock menu** and the native menu bar gets *Quick Fixes* and *Contacts* menus.
- **Finder gets seven more right-click Services:** Surface Scan, Save Disk Health Report, Tiny Backup Now, Free Up Space Here, Ask Mend AI About This, Install on iPhone (.ipa) and Restore iPhone from This Backup — next to the eight that were there. Windows Explorer and the Linux file managers get Tiny Backup Now, Save Disk Health Report, Free Up Space Here, Ask Mend AI and Install on iPhone too.
- **More notifications (only while Mend is not in front):** a repair or backup that ran longer than 20 s says when it finished or why it stopped (click opens the right page), a device plugged in while Mend is hidden says so, a device unplugged during a running job warns, and a new version announces itself.
- **Bad sectors and failing disks — more ways to repair:** *Rewrite bad sectors at an LBA* (zeros over just the sectors a self-test, the error log or a surface scan named, so the drive retires them — everything else stays), *Stop a failing disk freezing the computer* (SCT ERC 7 s), *Offline data collection* (refreshes the pending/reallocated counters), *Mark bad blocks in ext4 (keeps data)* (`e2fsck -c`), *Re-check bad clusters* (`CHKDSK /b`), *Deep repair* (`Repair-Volume -OfflineScanAndFix`), *Continue a rescue* from its ddrescue map and *Open a rescued image* read-only, *Read one sector by LBA*, *NVMe log* and *NVMe self-test*, Btrfs and ZFS scrubs, XFS and F2FS repairs, *Fix an NTFS volume on Linux* (`ntfsfix`), *Write caches to disk*, the ext bad-block list. Disk Health's rescue panel gained the matching steps; the Fix Library has eight more disk problems for every file system and media kind (≈ 1,000 new entries).
- **70 more software fixes:** macOS — Wi-Fi off/on, rebuild network settings, clear app caches, restart sharing, reset privacy permissions, rebuild the driver cache, reload login agents, Spotlight for one volume, swap usage, library cache (Intel), Quick Look previews, locate database, full Bluetooth reset. Windows — flush DNS, restart Explorer/sound/Bluetooth/network adapters, clear the print queue, rebuild font/icon/thumbnail caches, rebuild Search, clean temp files, repair WMI, sync the clock, reset BITS, re-register the Store and built-in apps, restore power plans, reset the firewall/hosts/proxy, repair Volume Shadow Copy, memory test. Linux — restart sound/Bluetooth/network, font cache, clock, trim logs, clean package caches, repair Flatpak, refresh snaps, clean temp, reset swap, regenerate locales, reset “open with”, clear GPU caches, check fstab, repair the package database. System Repair groups them by what feels broken.
- **Eight layouts for the Fix Library** — List, Cards, Compact, Tiles, Board (columns by category), Timeline, Magazine and Masonry — remembered between runs; an opened entry spreads across the row in every layout. Checked at 560, 640, 760 and 980 px: nothing overlaps or scrolls sideways.
- **Twenty new sounds with their own drawings** (bad sector, remap, scrub, freeze/thaw, quick panel, update found / up to date, layout, Finder, Dock, notification, quit, TRIM, self-test, Pour, cache, network, rewind) and a picture for every sound that had none (ticks, pops, pages, tabs, stars, steps, gauges, folders, clocks, keys…): 119 vector scenes for 131 sounds. Small UI sounds draw only in *Lively* and never more than a few a second. The colour audit still finds no hue between 280° and 350° anywhere.
- **Smaller start-up:** the owner panel and the quick panel are separate chunks loaded only by their own windows; the main bundle lost 150 KB.

- **The Linux AppImage ships again — packed without emulation:** linuxdeploy could not run under emulation on the Mac, so `scripts/appimage-cross.sh` builds the x86_64 AppImage natively from the amd64 `.deb` and the amd64 sysroot: every needed library found with readelf (linuxdeploy's exact exclude list), the tray-icon and SVG libraries it opens at run time, GTK input modules, pixbuf loaders, GIO modules and schemas with their caches, the WebKitGTK helper processes with the same relative-path patch Tauri applies, rpaths set with patchelf, squashed behind the official type-2 runtime and signed with the updater key. Verified on a clean Debian with no WebKitGTK installed: Mend and both WebKit processes run and the window renders.
- **iPhone backups that never finished are named as such:** a backup folder with Info.plist but no Manifest.db is an interrupted backup (Mend quit, cable out, phone locked), not “not an iPhone backup”. Data & export now says so with the state the backup recorded (Status.plist, read from binary plists too), marks it *incomplete* in the backup list, accepts the folder above a `<UDID>` folder, and offers **Back up again** right there — an interrupted backup resumes where it stopped.
- **iPhone battery health no longer shows 3 %:** newer iOS reports MaxCapacity/CurrentCapacity as percentages next to mAh values; dividing 100 % by the design mAh gave 3 %. Settings' own figure (MaximumCapacityPercent) is used when present, otherwise only capacities in the same unit as the design capacity, with a test for all three layouts.
- **Linux amd64 is cross-compiled now, not emulated:** one build image for the Mac's own architecture holds a full amd64 Debian sysroot (the GTK/WebKitGTK stack downloaded and unpacked under `/sysroot/amd64`, never executed) and the cross gcc; cargo links against it with `--sysroot`, so the amd64 `.deb` builds at native speed in a few minutes instead of 70+ under QEMU, where gcc crashed. Only the AppImage packer (linuxdeploy) still needs emulation and stays best-effort. Tested here with the mirror-image setup (x86_64 host → arm64 sysroot): a signed `Mend_arm64.deb` in 2m45s, ARM binary, correct NEEDED libraries and Depends.
- **amd64 Linux under Rosetta, not QEMU:** the first amd64 container build took 72 minutes under QEMU and its AppImage packer (linuxdeploy) failed. update.sh now switches Rosetta on itself — colima is restarted with `--vm-type vz --vz-rosetta`, Docker Desktop gets “Use Rosetta for x86_64/amd64 emulation” turned on and is restarted — and the AppImage is packed in a second, verbose step with `NO_STRIP`; if it still fails the `.deb` is published and latest.json keeps the previous AppImage instead of the whole release stopping.
- **Homebrew's docker CLI has no BuildKit:** `docker build` fell back to the legacy builder and rejected `--progress`. update.sh now installs `docker-buildx` and links it as a CLI plugin (Docker Desktop users already have it), and only passes `--progress=plain` when buildx is there. Finished Windows/Linux installers for the current version now survive a rerun (release/ is no longer wiped whole).
- **Linux builds on the Mac, fixed and tested:** the build packages are now installed once into a reusable image (`scripts/linux-build.Dockerfile` + `scripts/linux-deps.sh`) instead of on every run; apt's real error is printed when something fails (it was hidden behind `dpkg returned an error code (1)`), with an automatic repair-and-retry and a workaround for the emulator crash that most often breaks amd64 package installs on Apple silicon; Node.js falls back to the official nodejs.org build if NodeSource fails; the container gets `CI=true` (the Tauri CLI rejects `CI=1`); arm64 builds first (native, fast); each architecture builds into its own folder with a kept Rust cache and crate volume, so reruns are quick; installers already built for this version are kept on a rerun.
- **Windows ARM64 build on a Mac:** `ring` assembles its ARM64 Windows code with plain `clang`, which rejects the clang-cl `/imsvc <dir>` header flags cargo-xwin sets (“no such file or directory: '/imsvc'”). update.sh now puts a tiny clang shim first in PATH during the Windows builds that rewrites `/imsvc` to `-isystem`.
- **Windows build on a Mac whose home folder has a space:** cargo-xwin keeps the Windows SDK under `~/Library/Caches/cargo-xwin` and joins its library paths into RUSTFLAGS with spaces, so a home like `/Users/Jagadeesh Kumar S` failed with “flag in rustflags must not contain its separator”. update.sh now keeps that cache at `/Users/Shared/cargo-xwin` (moving an already-downloaded SDK there) — `XWIN_CACHE_DIR` overrides it.
- **Every installer from the Mac, no GitHub Actions:** `update.sh` now installs what the Windows and Linux builds need when it is missing (cargo-xwin, NSIS, LLVM; Docker Desktop if present, otherwise colima + the docker CLI, started headless with Rosetta) and stops the release if a Windows or Linux build fails instead of quietly leaving it to CI. The CI workflow runs only with `--ci`; `--mac-only` publishes just the Mac builds on purpose. (The 1.0.10 run shipped only the DMGs because cargo-xwin, makensis and Docker were not on the Mac.)
- **Menu bar drop-downs:** new **Devices** (every connected phone/tablet, refresh, restart the USB service, back up now) and **Disks** (every disk with its health, full report, save a report for every disk, Disks & Partitions, duplicates) menus that follow what is connected; **Repair** and **Back Up** menus; View → Animations and View → Language (15 languages); Window → Mend Lives In (Dock / menu bar / background) and a test notification; Help → Star Mend on GitHub, Install with Pour (copies the two lines), Open the Log Folder, Helpers & Log.
- **`bash update.sh` no longer stops at the Rust tests on a Mac where Mend is running:** the single-instance test connected to the real `~/Mend/mend-<uid>.sock`, handed its arguments to the running app and reported a failure. It now uses a temporary socket (and a second test proves the hand-over round trip). Nothing had been published on 14 Oct because of it; the next run goes through.
- **Contacts → AI tidy (new tab):** short, meaningful names (drops emojis, numbers, "work/new/old", repeated words and shouting, keeps Tamil/Hindi/Arabic script) and notes summarised to two lines — proposed by the AI Mend already uses (a local model on the Mac keeps everything on the computer; the built-in free one otherwise), shown as before → after rows you tick before anything is saved. A summary that loses a phone number, date or amount is thrown away. Also in the right-click Repair menu.
- **Fixed the 1.0.9 crash that made Settings unreachable on the owner's Mac** (10 reports: `rc@index-CnL1QT0J.js` ReferenceError and the `insertBefore` NotFoundError that followed): the Settings dialog read a value before it was declared, so every open of Settings threw inside render and left the window half-drawn. Settings opens again for owner, Pro and free; the Playwright page-error hunt now covers every dialog in owner and Pro mode and in a non-Latin language.
- **Disk Health judged against real drives:** laptop and USB hard disks are rated on 300,000 start-stop cycles, not 50,000, and a worn counter never drags the estimate below 20 % by itself — only damage does (a WD10SPCX with 119,000 start-stops now reads about 60 % left, not 0 %). A four-state **SMART status** — OK · Warning · Failing · Failed — stands beside the gauges and in the report, so a Seagate with 456 remapped, 1,064 pending and 10,000 reported uncorrectable errors says FAILED like the drive itself does. A USB drive that gives no SMART data shows “no data”, never “100 % good”. New findings: heads parking many times an hour (→ APM 254), spinning down all day (→ standby off), minutes spent over the temperature limit, thousands of CRC errors flagged as cable/bridge. Thousands of CRC errors cost at most 8 points.
- **Save report for each disk:** a Save report button on every disk card (the model in the file name), and Save each disk / the right-click “Save every disk report” write one file per disk from one dialog — text, Markdown or web page.
- **More disk repairs:** stop the heads parking (APM 254), stop the drive spinning down, turn the write cache on, the drive's temperature history (SCT) as a sparkline, CHKDSK /spotfix and /scan /forceofflinefix on Windows; 1,200 new disk fixes and 36 new Windows, Linux and Android software fixes — the Fix Library is now 16,826 problems.
- **Account features from the updated accounts API:** check a code before signing in (plan, Pro days, expiry), the account summary, every subscription with a cancel-at-period-end button, gift a spare code to someone by email, licences per app, rename this computer.
- **Owner Panel → ipconfig dashboard:** a Sync to dashboard button registers Mend (`/owner/hello`) and pushes installs, codes, subscriptions and crash reports (`/owner/sync`); needs `APPS_API_KEY` in `.env`, pushed to the Worker by update.sh with `wrangler secret bulk`.
- **Every installer is built on the Mac** — macOS (DMG, both chips), Windows x64 + ARM64 (cargo-xwin + NSIS), Linux amd64 + arm64 (.deb + AppImage in Docker) — and pushed to the GitHub release and Cloudflare R2 by `update.sh`; the GitHub Actions run is skipped when everything was built locally (CI minutes are no longer needed). `--stores` adds the Mac App Store .pkg and the Microsoft Store upload when the store keys are in `.env` (docs/STORES.md).
- **Pour everywhere:** both READMEs and the product page install Mend with `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/pour/install | sh` then `pour install --cask mend` (Windows: pour-windows-x86_64.exe); no Homebrew formula, cask or tap. The READMEs ask readers to star the repository.
- Haiku: still no installer — Tauri's window engine has no Haiku port (documented in the README).

- **One account for every build and store:** Mend Pro → Your account signs in with an email code (or password) to the accounts service, asks for this computer's licence — an Ed25519-signed token bound to the machine — and verifies it locally; refreshed every 12 hours, good for 14 days offline. Reinstalls on the same computer never use a second seat; at the limit the dialog lists the computers so one can be deactivated right there; “Deactivate this computer”, rename a computer, redeem a gift code into the account, the plan with days left and seats used. Anonymous daily ping and crash signatures go to the same service (Settings → Privacy switches the ping off).
- **Disk Health shows the whole disk:** used · free · total with one bar segment per volume (APFS containers counted once, external and Windows drives included — `df -k` fills in what diskutil and lsblk leave out), the volumes below it, and the general information (device, capacity, type, connection, partition map, volumes, serial, model, firmware) on every card before any SMART read. A free-space threshold (5–20 %) warns in the card, in Checkup and as a desktop notification.
- **Bad sectors and failing disks:** a rescue plan on any disk that fails, has pending or remapped sectors or a low score — stop writing, back up, clone with ddrescue (new), remap (CHKDSK /r, badblocks -n, or “Zero and remap” on a Mac — new), check again. New repairs: read-only surface scan on every OS, conveyance self-test, stop a self-test, self-test progress, the drive's error log + self-test log + device statistics + SATA link errors, SMART through USB bridges (SAT, ASMedia, JMicron, Realtek), deep offline file-system repair, Windows disk/volume status. A help card explains the SAT SMART driver external USB disks need on macOS, with the project page, install and removal steps. 1,440 new disk fixes (bad sectors, CRC errors, failing self-tests, growing error logs, SSD wear…).
- **Duplicates (new page, ⌘D):** identical files by content (size → first 64 KiB → full SHA-256), look-alike pictures (a 64-bit difference hash from a 9×8 thumbnail made by sips / System.Drawing / ImageMagick / ffmpeg, strict · normal · loose), and duplicates in cloud storages through rclone (size + checksum; Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3…). Keep the newest, oldest, largest, shortest path or the one in Pictures; everything else goes to the Trash / Recycle Bin — never the last copy of a set; cloud copies only when asked; a report; 50 files per run on the free plan.
- **Desktop notifications that open Mend:** backups done or failed, a disk warning, free space running low, a device connected — macOS Notification Centre (a click opens Mend on the right page), Windows toasts (the `mend://open/<page>` link opens it), Linux `notify-send` with an Open button. Settings → Notifications has a test. Only while Mend is hidden or in the background; in front, a toast instead.
- **Right-click in Finder, File Explorer and Linux file managers:** macOS Services with nothing to install — Check Disk Health, Repair Disk, Back Up, Find Duplicates, Import Contacts, Fix .vcf, Browse iPhone Backup, Open in Mend; Windows per-user verbs for files, folders, drives and .vcf/.csv; GNOME Files scripts, Dolphin, Nemo and Thunar entries (Settings → Right-click). Files dropped on the Dock icon and `open -a Mend file` go to the right page too.
- **Menu-bar icon, Dock menu and in-app right-click with drop-downs:** Devices ▸ (the connected phones), Disks ▸ (with health %), Go to ▸, Back up ▸, Repair ▸, Appearance ▸ (theme, sounds, animations, text size, sidebar), Language ▸ — the lists follow what is connected. Device cards, disk cards and contact rows have their own entries. Tall menus fold into columns instead of scrolling.
- **Presence:** a “Keep Mend running in the background” switch; with it off, or with the Dock icon alone, closing the last window quits Mend completely. The menu-bar icon is a drawn template image (no PNG decoder in the app).
- **15,003 repairs:** +1,440 disk, +550 Windows (apps, installers, Store, Explorer, activation, Defender, 100 % disk, Start menu, taskbar, updates, drivers, USB, printers, Bluetooth, display, sound, PIN, malware, C: full, Recycle Bin, Office, OneDrive, sleep, shares), +276 Android (apps keep stopping, Play Store, WebView, notifications, storage, lag, updates, battery, charging, Wi-Fi, mobile data, Bluetooth, GPS, touch, flicker, speaker, mic, camera, PIN, FRP, USB debugging, MTP, keyboard, Chrome, gallery, SD card, hotspot, fingerprint, selling), +441 iPad, +143 Apple Watch, +238 Linux (package locks, dependencies, GPG, no space, login loop, sound, scaling, Wi-Fi after a kernel update, DNS, VPN, failed services, time, Snap/Flatpak, permissions, tearing, touchpad, printers, slow boot, fonts).
- **Checkup:** volumes under the free-space threshold, bad sectors on any disk, and a reminder to look for duplicates.
- **Vector scenes with every sound:** 50 self-drawing SVG scenes (phones, disks, backups, contacts, repairs, rescue, duplicates, notifications…) appear near the pointer with their sound; Settings → Animations: Off / Subtle (the big moments) / Lively.
- **Small windows:** the window now goes down to 640 × 420; findings, tables and the deep disk report fold instead of scrolling sideways (checked at 640 and 760 px on every screen).
- **Owner Panel → Computers:** the computer's name with each install, CSV export and Forget.
- **Smaller app:** the single-instance plugin (D-Bus on Linux) is replaced by a unix socket on macOS, Linux and FreeBSD; the PNG decoder feature is gone.
- **Releases from the Mac:** `update.sh` builds the Windows installers (cargo-xwin + NSIS) and the Linux packages (Docker) on the Mac itself — no CI minutes — and `--stores` makes the Mac App Store package and submits the Windows installer to the Microsoft Store when the keys are in `.env` (docs/STORES.md).
- **Fixes:** the checkout window title showed the old prices; the Pro dialog's code field stays for the Worker codes.


- **Backups that carry on after a dropped connection:** “Could not receive from mobilebackup2 (-4) … Backup Aborted” is now explained (the iPhone locked or slept, the cable moved or a hub dropped power) and the backup continues by itself, incrementally, up to three tries — in the app and in `mend backup`. Apple Configurator's “Failed to connect to the device (-2)” right after asks you to reconnect first. A new button restarts the iPhone connection service (usbmuxd, or Apple Mobile Device Service on Windows). Progress bars no longer fill the log with hundreds of identical lines.
- **Separate, incremental backups for every device:** each kind of data on its own — iPhone/iPad contacts, messages, WhatsApp, calls, notes, calendar, Safari, bookmarks, voicemail, photos, music, ringtones, books and recordings; Android contacts (each account), camera photos, pictures, WhatsApp media, downloads, documents, music, movies and recordings; and every contacts account on this computer. Data is saved as a new version only when it changed; files are mirrored, copying only what's new or changed. “Back up everything separately”, a folder of your choice (drive or NAS), and an overview of every device on the Tiny Backups page.
- **Fix backed-up contacts and add them to iCloud:** choose contacts saved from phones and backups; Mend fixes them, merges duplicates, skips people already in the account, saves a .vcf copy and adds the rest to iCloud, Google or any internet account.
- **Menu-bar (tray) icon and where Mend shows itself:** Dock and menu bar, Dock only, menu bar only, or background only (taskbar and tray on Windows and Linux). The menu-bar icon has the main commands; in menu-bar and background modes closing the window keeps Mend running, and starting Mend again shows it. Only one Mend runs at a time.
- **Schedules everywhere:** when there's no systemd user session (some ChromeOS containers) and on FreeBSD, automatic backups use cron.
- **Layouts:** separate-backup tiles use round buttons so names fit at every width; the overlap checker now accounts for clipped text.

- **11,570 repairs for 16 kinds of device:** the Fix Library adds iPad (21 model families), Apple Watch (13 models), Apple TV, AirPods, HomePod, Vision Pro, Android (12 makers), Windows 10, 11 and 11 on Arm (on 9 PC makers), Linux (16 distributions), ChromeOS, FreeBSD and Haiku, and grows disks to 3,039 (ReFS, ZFS, F2FS, M.2 SATA, RAID/NAS volumes, Thunderbolt docks and disk images). Each problem uses that model's own buttons, menus, recovery keys and commands, and says whether Standard Repair, Full Repair, steps or a part fixes it. Every family has its own animated picture and sound.
- **Device files (iMazing-style):** a Files tab browses an iPhone or iPad like a drive — photos, music files, ringtones, books, recordings — over USB or Wi-Fi; copy anything to the computer; Quick Transfer files or folders onto the device or into an app's Documents; new folder, rename, delete and a right-click menu.
- **Configurator:** a Manage tab builds configuration profiles (Wi-Fi, 16 restrictions, Kiosk Mode, web clips, passcode rules), shows the colour-coded XML, saves, signs (keychain certificate) and installs them on one or every connected device; supervises a freshly erased device; removes profiles; backs up, installs an .ipa on or restarts every connected device at once.
- **App downloads:** download App Store apps as .ipa files with your own Apple Account (ipatool) and install them on this device or all of them. Apps that share files are marked and open in the Files tab.
- **Automatic backups:** daily or weekly, over USB or Wi-Fi, one device or all, even while Mend is closed (launchd, systemd timer or Task Scheduler). Each backup keeps a snapshot (an APFS clone on a Mac), archived snapshots are kept forever, old ones are cleaned by count and age, and any drive or NAS can hold them. Backups can now be incremental.
- **Evidence reports:** Messages, WhatsApp and every other kind of backup data export as a printable report with case details, the device's serial and IMEI, SHA-256 of the source database and the backup manifest, a fingerprint of the rows, every message's metadata and attachments, page numbers and signature lines. New exports: message attachments, notes attachments, ringtones and books.
- **Command line:** `Mend --cli` (or `mend` after Settings › Command line): devices, info, backup (with snapshots and cleaning), backups, snapshots, export, extract, files and screenshot.
- **15 languages:** English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Hindi and Tamil for menus, tabs and buttons; Mend AI answers in the chosen language. Follows the computer's language on first start.
- **Right-click menus everywhere and a Dock menu:** text fields, selected text, links, logs and code, sidebar places and fixes each get their own items, plus every app command. Right-click Mend in the Dock for Find a Repair, Checkup, Mend AI, each area, Back Up iPhone Now and Full Disk Report.
- **Closing the window quits Mend completely** (also ⌘W and the new Quit item), stopping running helpers; nothing stays behind in the Dock.
- **Disk Health art no longer crowds the text:** the SSD/HDD picture sits in its own tile with a label, clear of the health ring and the heading.
- **More colour:** commands to type and device and system names get their own colours, the XML of profiles is colour-coded, folder paths alternate colours, and menu icons each take a colour.
- **More sounds:** device files, transfers, snapshots, schedules, profiles, evidence, printing, languages, Kiosk Mode, app downloads, menus, quitting, every connected device, and a motif per device family.

- **Standard Repair and Full Repair for macOS:** the same two levels as iPhone. Standard Repair makes a restore point and reinstalls macOS over itself — files, apps and settings stay. Full Repair erases the Mac and installs a clean macOS (Erase All Content and Settings on Apple silicon). Pick the installer in the new “Standard & Full Repair” tab.
- **4,109 fixes, and 1,000+ for every repair:** the Fix Library now holds 1,223 iPhone & iPad, 1,159 Mac, 1,307 disk and 420 contact problems. Each repair screen shows exactly what it resolves:
  - **iPhone:** Standard Repair 1,118, Deep Repair 1,126.
  - **Mac:** Standard Repair 1,107, Full Repair 1,115.
  - **Disks:** Standard Repair (check and repair the file system) 1,024; Full Repair (erase and reformat) 1,280 — every common file system on every kind of drive, with that file system's own repair commands.
  - **Contacts:** Fix everything 336, Rebuild 420 — every real problem kind in each of 14 kinds of source.
  - It also shows, honestly, which problems need steps or hardware instead. Tap a number to see the list. The Library has new Disks and Contacts tabs.
- **Disk health beyond DriveDx:** “Full report” reads every SMART/NVMe indicator, then shows health and lifetime-left gauges, years left at 8 h a day, projected endurance, data written per powered-on day, temperature against its limits, read/write statistics since start-up, errors and retries, and a finding for each problem with the repair that fixes it. Export the report as text, Markdown or a web page.
- **Repairs for bad sectors and worn disks:** remap bad sectors (chkdsk /r on Windows, a non-destructive badblocks pass on Linux), a write test that forces remapping (Linux, erases), zero-and-remap for Mac disks (erases), TRIM (trimforce, fstrim, ReTrim), long self-tests and turning SMART on. Heavy daily writing is flagged with what causes it.
- **Contact manager, Kontact style — every account separately, like Contacts on the Mac:** a side pane lists every source and nothing is ever merged:
  - **This Mac:** every account in the Mac's Contacts — any number of iCloud, Google, Outlook/Exchange and Yahoo accounts, plus On My Mac — read and edited through Apple's Contacts framework.
  - **iCloud and CardDAV accounts** signed in here (Fastmail, Yahoo, Nextcloud…).
  - **Every iPhone and iPad**, read from its backup with photos and groups.
  - **Every account on every Android phone**, each Google account and the SIM listed separately.
  - **Mend's own library:** address books kept as .vcf in ~/Mend/Contacts/Library, with the last 30 versions of each kept so any earlier version can be brought back.
  - **Open files:** .vcf, Google or Outlook .csv, and Thunderbird .ldif.
  - **Overview page:** totals, problems, birthdays this month, a search across every source (results stay labelled by source), "Load every source" and "Save every source to the library".
  - **Each source has tabs:** Contacts, Groups (the Mac's own groups or vCard categories), Birthdays & dates (with a calendar .ics), Fix everything, Duplicates, Numbers, and Copy & move (to any account, a library book, an Android phone or a file).
- **Every contact field:** prefix, middle and maiden names, phonetic names, department and role, any number of phones, emails, addresses (with a map link), websites, messaging (WhatsApp, Telegram, Skype…), social profiles, related people, birthday and other dates, groups and notes. Apple's labels are kept, so cards look the same on the iPhone.
- **Phone numbers in detail:** every number is checked with Google's numbering rules for every country. Mend shows:
  - the country and its flag;
  - the type of line: mobile, landline, toll-free, VoIP…;
  - whether the number can really exist;
  - its international, E.164 and local forms, each copyable;
  - Call and WhatsApp buttons, and a one-click fix to the international form.
- **Any number of devices at once:** every connected iPhone, iPad, Android and Mac — in normal, Recovery or DFU mode — gets its own tabs, and repairs run side by side. Changing tab or screen never stops a running job.
- **iPhone data (iMazing-style):** browse and export Messages, WhatsApp, call history, contacts, notes, Safari, calendar and voicemail from a backup (CSV or a printable page), copy out photos, voice memos and WhatsApp media, check a backup for spyware with MVT, and transfer one iPhone to another.
- **Repair another Mac:** revive or restore an Apple silicon Mac in DFU from this Mac with Apple Configurator, with key guides for every Mac; or share its disk and run First Aid, back it up or reinstall macOS onto it. iPhone repair also works through Apple Configurator when idevicerestore can't be installed.
- **No overlaps in small windows:** every screen and tab, including every Contacts view, was checked at 560, 760, 900, 1000 and 1240 px wide.
- **Hard-disk life left:** hard drives have no wear counter, so Mend now estimates their life. It weighs power-on hours against the usual service life of desktop, laptop or NAS drives, head load cycles and start-stops against their ratings, and any bad sectors, then shows which of these sets the figure. It appears as a gauge, a breakdown, years left at 8 hours a day or 24/7, and a line in the exported report.
- **Full report for all disks:** one button reads every disk. A Disk Health setting (on by default) shows the full report for every disk whenever the page opens. The full report now works on Windows too (with smartmontools). TRIM is offered only for SSDs.
- **How each repair fixes problems:** iPhone and Mac repair screens explain step by step what Standard and Full (Deep) Repair replace, what they keep and why that fixes problems. Every fix in the Fix Library is marked with what resolves it: Standard Repair, Full Repair, the steps, or hardware.
- **iPhone Apps tab fixed:** it uses the current ideviceinstaller (`list --xml`) and falls back to older versions. It lists your apps, Apple's apps or all, sorts by name or size, and shows the real error if the iPhone doesn't answer.
- **No more caps:** long lists (contacts, chats, backup files, Android apps, unreadable files) load more as you scroll instead of stopping at a few hundred. iPhone Safari and calendar history is read in full. Any number of iPhones, iPads and Macs can be connected and repaired at the same time.
- **Helpers are found where they really are:**
  - **Apple Configurator from the App Store is detected straight away.** Mend uses its tool from inside the app (or finds the app with Spotlight), so "Install Automation Tools" is no longer needed.
  - **No more "already installed" loop for libimobiledevice and ideviceinstaller.** Mend shows exactly which commands are missing and installs only those Homebrew packages; if Homebrew already has a package, it relinks it instead of reinstalling. ideviceinstaller (for the Apps tab) is now its own helper.
  - **Mend notices installs by itself.** After you press Install it checks every few seconds, and again when you switch back to it — no "Check again" needed.
- **idevicerestore installs reliably:** Mend writes its own build script, which clones libimobiledevice, idevicerestore and ideviceinstaller from GitHub (retrying), builds the newest versions into ~/Mend/limd without sudo, and installs only the Homebrew packages that are missing — no more is.gd link (blocked on some networks) or "already installed" warnings. With Apple Configurator installed, idevicerestore is optional and shown as covered.
- **iPhone backups fixed:**
  - Mend's newest tool build fixes backups that fail with old libimobiledevice on recent iOS.
  - **Back up with Apple Configurator** is a second route that works with every iOS version.
  - A failed backup is explained in plain words, with buttons that fix it: Trust again, build the newest tools, back up with Apple Configurator, choose another folder.
- **Owner Panel → Active devices:** who is using Mend right now, today, this week and this month, on a live radar, with versions, systems, countries and a device list. The data comes from an anonymous heartbeat every 30 minutes: a hashed machine id, version, system and plan, never an IP address.
- **New features:**
  - **Health over time:** disk health, life left and iPhone battery capacity are kept day by day and drawn as lines.
  - **Daily disk watch** (on by default): Mend re-checks every disk once a day while it's open and warns if health drops.
  - **Repair history** for every device.
  - **QR codes** for contacts.
  - **"Sell or give away" checklists** for iPhone and Mac.
- **Mend Pro is now ₹4,000 a month or ₹6,000 a year.**
- **More colour and sound:** every tab has its own colour, and names start in colour. A new animated Contacts overview shows your sources orbiting a contact card. Gauges and date badges are animated. New sounds: sync, library book, dial, a birthday tune, gauge sweep, a wrench when you press Install, and a chime when a helper is ready. Button icons, table columns, fact labels and helper rows have their own colours; new animated pictures — a spinning hard disk or flickering SSD on every disk, an iPhone streaming into a backup drive (broken link when it fails), a toolbox with turning gears while helpers install, an active-devices radar — and new sounds for platters, flash chips and backup streams; section subtitles colour their numbers and paths, and an animated toolbox shows while a helper installs.
- **Checkup (⇧⌘C):** one button checks disks, free space, memory, security, battery, sleep, firewall, Time Machine, updates, recent errors and every connected phone — read-only — and gives a score with a Fix button for anything that needs attention.
- **Fix Library tools:** tick off steps as you go, save fixes with a star, mark a problem “It's fixed!”, filter by Saved, One-click or Fixed, and copy the steps to send to someone.
- **Repair report:** Helpers & Log → Export report saves the checkup, devices, disks, fixed problems and recent repairs as a Markdown file.
- **macOS keeps Mend's permissions after updates:** Mac builds are now signed with one permanent identity, so “Mend would like to access files on a removable volume” and the other permission prompts are asked once — not after every update. The prompts also explain why Mend asks.
- **More colour, no pink:** brackets change colour with each nesting level, section titles and borders take their section's colour, headings and dialog titles are tinted, and keys, numbers and file paths stand out everywhere.
- **More graphics, motion and sound:** gauges that sweep to their value, a temperature bar, a cable pulse between two Macs when one is found in DFU, chat bubbles for messages, colour-coded problem cards in the contact fixer; a radar sweep for the Checkup, an animated Mac being reinstalled, platform icons orbiting the startup logo, a slow colour aurora behind every screen, a colour sweep when you change screens, and new sounds — a note per area, radar, tick-off, star, “fixed” fanfare and report.

### Install

- **macOS** (Apple silicon and Intel): `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/updates/mend/install.sh | bash`
- **Windows** (PowerShell): `irm https://ipconfig.co.network/updates/mend/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Linux** (AppImage): `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/updates/mend/install.sh | bash` — add `-s -- --deb` for the .deb

First launch on macOS after a manual DMG install: `xattr -cr /Applications/Mend.app` (Mend is ad-hoc signed, not notarized).
